---
title: "check-code-messages.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only check that keeps warnings and non-output messages
out of rendered code.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-10-26) is that rendered code shows its output
and nothing else.
The commonest case is the "`geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'" message,
which disappears when the call names its `method` and `formula`.

The source lint flags, in the R chunks of `.qmd`, `.Rmd` and `.md` files
and in `.R` files:

- `geom_smooth()` or `stat_smooth()` missing `method` or `formula`;
- `geom_histogram()` or `stat_bin()` with none of `bins`, `binwidth` and
  `breaks`.

It reads a call across lines up to its closing parenthesis,
and reports a call only when the pull request adds a line inside it.
Prose, inline code and non-R chunks are not read.

## Scanning a rendered site

The `check-code-messages` composite action also takes `site-dir`,
a directory of rendered HTML such as `_site`.
It flags every Quarto `cell-output-stderr` block,
where knitr, reticulate and Jupyter put all warnings and messages,
and the text of the two messages above.
The scan always covers the whole directory,
so run it after a render, and set `site-ignore` to skip pages.
The reusable workflow does not render, so a repository that wants the scan
calls the action in its own render job.

## Inputs

| Input | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `globs` | Space-separated pathspecs to lint (default `*.qmd *.Rmd *.R`) |
| `fail` | Fail on a finding instead of warning (default `false`) |
| `whole-tree` | Lint every tracked file, not just a PR's additions |
| `runs-on`, `python-version` | Runner and Python version |
